findings.what: No code head of this pull request has completed CI since round 2. Each round's push CANCELS the previous round's run before its heaviest lanes and the required `ci-ok` finish.
findings.evidence: Run 41188931937 (round 4's head db64c79daa38, created 09:30:03Z) ended `cancelled`, updated 12:40:36Z — the moment round 5's push landed. Run 41202161046 (round 5's head 703782de8f2b, created 12:40:34Z) ended `cancelled`, updated 14:52:38Z — the moment this round's push landed. That second run did get 24 lanes to `success` before it was cut: lint, typecheck, test, contracts, envoy-client, envoy-go-race, envoy-go-race-api, envoy-go-race-docs, envoy-e2e-local, envoy-infra-go, envoy-plugin, envoy-session-stall, listener-server-change, pi-envoy, pi-legion, pi-shared, claude-envoy, dispatch-browser-multiprocess, dispatch-memory, dispatch-multiprocess, docs/build, worker-image/build, changes, ci-filters. The four it never finished are exactly the long ones and the aggregate: `ci-ok`, `envoy-go`, `dispatch`, `envoy-smoke`. `envoy-go` is the lane that covers the kept lane's own Go package, and `ci-ok` is what main's ruleset requires. Both last succeeded at round 2's head 4f6e9985b979 (run 41163858951), which predates the claim-forward-confirm design, the handover rewrite, the sweep and the Dispatch keep reversal. This round's run 41212135030 (created 14:52:18Z) was still `queued` at 15:16Z, 24 minutes in, with only `changes` queued.
findings.whyItMatters: The merge gate needs `ci-ok` green at the head the merger builds READY from. On the present cadence that can never happen: a round takes about two hours of queue and lanes, and the next push arrives first and cancels it. This is scheduling, not a defect in the change, and it is the architect's to break — one round where nothing is pushed until the run drains would settle it. It does not fail this round: every acceptance line is proven live, and I ran the kept-lane Go tests and their mutations locally myself.
